title: Kabel Laut Palapa Ring Terdampak Gempa, Satria-1 Jaga Internet Warga - detikInet
snippet: Kabel Laut Palapa Ring Terdampak Gempa, Satria-1 Jaga Internet Warga detikInet
article_text:
Agus Tri Haryanto - detikInet
Badan Aksesibilitas Telekomunikasi dan Informasi (Bakti) Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Komdigi) mengoptimalkan kapasitas internet berbasis satelit Satria-1 guna menjaga layanan telekomunikasi di Kepulauan Sangihe, Talaud, dan Sitaro, Sulawesi Utara. Langkah ini dilakukan selama proses restorasi kabel optik bawah laut Palapa Ring Tengah yang terdampak aktivitas tektonik.
Optimalisasi dilakukan setelah terdeteksi gangguan pada sebagian serat optik di segmen Melonguane-Morotai. Pemerintah menegaskan proses restorasi merupakan langkah preventif untuk menjaga keandalan jaringan dan mencegah gangguan layanan yang lebih luas, sementara akses internet masyarakat tetap ditopang melalui jaringan satelit Satria-1.
Pelaksana Tugas Direktur Infrastruktur Bakti Komdigi, Darien Aldiano, mengatakan pemerintah telah menyiapkan berbagai langkah mitigasi agar masyarakat tetap memperoleh akses telekomunikasi selama pekerjaan berlangsung.
SCROLL TO CONTINUE WITH CONTENT
"Kami menyampaikan permohonan maaf atas ketidaknyamanan yang dialami masyarakat terdampak di Kepulauan Sangihe, Talaud, dan Sitaro. Kami memastikan seluruh tim bekerja maksimal di lapangan untuk mempercepat pemulihan infrastruktur vital ini demi terwujudnya konektivitas yang berkualitas di seluruh pelosok Indonesia," ujar Darien dikutip Sabtu, 25/7/2026).
Sebagai antisipasi, Bakti meningkatkan kapasitas bandwidth pada 286 titik layanan Akses Internet yang selama ini telah beroperasi di wilayah terdampak dan terhubung melalui satelit Satria-1.
Rinciannya meliputi 106 titik di Kabupaten Kepulauan Sangihe, 132 titik di Kabupaten Kepulauan Talaud, serta 48 titik di Kabupaten Kepulauan Sitaro. Kapasitas internet di lokasi tersebut ditingkatkan menjadi 50 Mbps, 100 Mbps, hingga 150 Mbps sesuai kebutuhan masing-masing titik.
Layanan Akses Internet Bakti tersebut berada di berbagai fasilitas publik, seperti kantor pemerintahan, sekolah, puskesmas, rumah sakit, hingga fasilitas pertahanan dan keamanan. Selama proses restorasi berlangsung, masyarakat dapat memanfaatkan titik-titik tersebut untuk tetap mengakses layanan telekomunikasi dan internet.
Selain meningkatkan kapasitas, tim teknis juga melakukan pemantauan berkala terhadap pengalaman pengguna (user experience) guna memastikan layanan seperti browsing dan komunikasi digital tetap berjalan optimal.
Berdasarkan hasil investigasi teknis, anomali pada kabel laut Palapa Ring Tengah terjadi setelah serangkaian aktivitas gempa bumi di kawasan Melonguane-Morotai, termasuk gempa bermagnitudo 5,7 yang terjadi pada 26 Mei 2026.
Kerusakan terdeteksi berada di dasar laut dengan kedalaman sekitar 3.400 meter atau sekitar 95 kilometer dari Terminal Station Morotai.
Lokasi kerusakan yang berada di laut dalam membuat proses perbaikan membutuhkan kapal khusus yang memiliki kemampuan melakukan pemasangan dan penyambungan kabel bawah laut di kedalaman ekstrem.
Dalam rapat koordinasi yang melibatkan Direktorat Jenderal Infrastruktur Digital Komdigi, Bakti, Balai Monitoring Spektrum Frekuensi Radio, PT Len Telekomunikasi Indonesia, PT Surveyor Indonesia, operator telekomunikasi, serta sejumlah pemangku kepentingan lainnya, telah disepakati pembaruan jadwal pekerjaan ( Plan of Work ).
Sesuai rencana, kapal perbaikan akan berangkat dari Bitung menuju Morotai pada 28 Juli 2026 setelah seluruh dokumen administrasi dan perizinan pelayaran selesai diproses.
Selama proses penyambungan kabel, diperkirakan akan terdapat periode kritis layanan selama sekitar 12 hari. Apabila seluruh tahapan berjalan sesuai rencana, jaringan Palapa Ring Tengah ditargetkan kembali beroperasi penuh (Ready for Service) pada 11 Agustus 2026.
Bakti menyatakan akan terus menyampaikan perkembangan restorasi secara berkala melalui kanal komunikasi resmi serta memperkuat koordinasi dengan pemerintah daerah, aparat keamanan, dan operator telekomunikasi agar proses perbaikan berjalan sesuai jadwal.

title: Satria-1 dan Palapa Ring Jangkau Pelosok, Sinyal tak Lagi Dicari di Atas Pohon - Inilah.com
snippet: Satria-1 dan Palapa Ring Jangkau Pelosok, Sinyal tak Lagi Dicari di Atas Pohon Inilah.com
article_text:
cyberlife
Warga 3T dulu naik pohon demi sinyal. Kini BAKTI Komdigi menghubungkan Flores Timur hingga Parigi Moutong lewat Satria-1, Palapa Ring, dan BTS USO. (Foto: Antara)
Dulu, warga di pelosok Flores Timur harus memanjat pohon hanya untuk mendapat satu garis sinyal. Guru, petugas Puskesmas, sampai aparat desa menempuh jarak berkilometer demi mengirim laporan atau membuka informasi.
Pemandangan itu kini mulai berubah. Badan Aksesibilitas Telekomunikasi dan Informasi (BAKTI) Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital menggelar infrastruktur konektivitas hingga ke wilayah tertinggal, terdepan, dan terluar (3T). Cerita ini mengemuka dalam agenda BAKTI Media Connect 2026 di Jakarta, Rabu (12/8/2026).
Direktur Utama BAKTI Komdigi Fadhilah Mathar mengatakan percepatan konektivitas digital ditopang kombinasi jaringan darat dan satelit. Menurut perempuan yang akrab disapa Indah itu, kehadiran satelit membuat BAKTI bisa menjangkau wilayah yang semula sulit diakses jaringan biasa.
"Kehadiran Satria-1 ini membuat kita bisa menggabungkan solusi terestrial dengan solusi non-terestrial pada saat wilayah-wilayah itu memang masih sangat sulit," kata Indah.
BAKTI mengelola beberapa aset strategis secara terintegrasi. Di ruang angkasa, Satelit Republik Indonesia (Satria-1) berkapasitas 150 Gbps menopang konektivitas sekolah, puskesmas, kantor pemerintah, hingga pos TNI/Polri di wilayah 3T sejak 2024.
Di darat dan laut, Palapa Ring menjadi tulang punggung jaringan serat optik di wilayah non-komersial. Infrastruktur ini membentang 12.148 kilometer dan melayani 131 titik Network Operation Center (NOC) di 57 kabupaten/kota di Indonesia bagian Barat, Tengah, dan Timur.
Konektivitas diperkuat lewat BAKTI AKSI yang menyediakan internet gratis di lebih dari 31.864 titik layanan publik. Sementara BAKTI SINYAL membangun BTS 4G dan BTS Universal Service Obligation (USO) hingga 6.747 titik lokasi di wilayah 3T dan perbatasan, dengan dana dari APBN dan kontribusi USO.
Dampaknya terasa di Kabupaten Flores Timur, Nusa Tenggara Timur, daerah kepulauan yang rawan bencana. Di sini, BAKTI membangun enam BTS dan sekitar 262 akses internet untuk kantor pemerintah, desa, sekolah, dan fasilitas kesehatan.
Kepala Dinas Kominfo Flores Timur Silvester Suban Toa Kabelen mengenang masa ketika warga harus berjalan kaki atau naik motor demi mencari titik bersinyal. "Kadang naik pohon karena di bawah tidak ada sinyal, jadi harus naik pohon," ujarnya.
Meski begitu, akses yang membaik memunculkan tantangan baru: kapasitas jaringan. Kepala SMAN 1 Titehena Konradus Kudarto mengatakan sekolahnya kesulitan bandwidth saat seluruh siswa mengakses sistem ujian bersamaan. Ia mencontohkan sekitar 450 siswa ditambah 50 guru dan pengawas memakai jaringan secara serentak saat asesmen.
"Saya datang dengan harapan besar supaya ada peningkatan kapasitasnya," kata Konradus. Kebutuhan sekolah, katanya, bukan lagi sekadar ada sinyal, melainkan kapasitas yang memadai.
Manfaat konektivitas juga menyentuh sektor ekonomi. Di Kabupaten Parigi Moutong, Sulawesi Tengah, internet membantu petani mengakses informasi harga komoditas. Posisi tawar petani terhadap tengkulak pun menguat.
Pelaksana Tugas Kepala Dinas Kominfo Parigi Moutong Khairuddin mengatakan warga pegunungan kini bisa mengakses informasi dari tingkat provinsi hingga kecamatan. Kepala Desa Baina Barat Yuslan menambahkan, warga dapat membandingkan harga dan mencari pembeli terbaik sebelum menjual hasil tani.
Pelaku UMKM ikut merasakan dampaknya. Menurut Yuslan, warga memanfaatkan media sosial untuk mempromosikan produk dan menerima pesanan dari luar desa. "Mereka posting di foto, kemudian dikirim di media sosial," tuturnya.

title: BAKTI Komdigi Sukses Sediakan 30 Ribu Akses Internet Berkat Satelit Satria-1 - Suara.com
snippet: BAKTI Komdigi Sukses Sediakan 30 Ribu Akses Internet Berkat Satelit Satria-1 Suara.com
article_text:
Available On
Dicky Prastya
Suara.com - Badan Aksesibilitas Telekomunikasi dan Informasi Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital atau BAKTI Komdigi mengatakan kalau mereka berhasil membangun 30.017 titik akses internet berkat kehadiran Satelit Republik Indonesia 1 atau Satria-1 .
"Saat ini sudah ada 30.000 titik lokasi akses internet di Indonesia," kata Direktur Utama BAKTI Komdigi, Fadhilah Mathar saat konferensi pers di Stasiun Bumi (Gateway) Satria-1 Satelit Nusantara Tiga, di Cikarang, Rabu (10/12/2025).
Perempuan yang akrab disapa Indah ini bercerita, Satria-1 membuat BAKTI Komdigi lebih terukur saat melakukan pengembangan pembangunan titik internet di layanan publik di Indonesia.
Sebelum ada Satria-1, BAKTI Komdigi hanya bisa membangun sekitar 1.000 titik akses internet atau maksimal 2.000 titik dalam waktu setahun. "Dalam satu tahun yang dulunya kami hanya bisa membangun sekitar 1.000, paling banyak 2.000 titik itu dalam satu tahun masa operasional Satria-1 itu kita bisa lebih dari 20.000 titik," lanjutnya.
Diketahui SATRIA-1 merupakan proyek Kerja Sama Pemerintah dan Badan Usaha (KPBU) yang menyediakan satelit berkapasitas 150 Gbps untuk memperkuat konektivitas digital, khususnya di wilayah tertinggal, terdepan, terluar (3T), serta lokasi prioritas layanan publik yang beroperasi sejak tahun 2024.
Dengan total investasi sekitar Rp 6,42 triliun dan skema Build–Operate–Transfer (BOT), proyek ini dilaksanakan oleh PT Satelit Nusantara Tiga (SNT) sebagai Badan Usaha Pelaksana (BUP), dengan Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Komdigi) selaku Penanggung Jawab Proyek Kerja Sama (PJPK), di mana sebagian wewenangnya didelegasikan kepada BAKTI Komdigi.
Hingga 7 Desember 2025, SATRIA-1 telah menghubungkan 30.017 titik layanan publik di seluruh Indonesia, termasuk sekolah, puskesmas, fasilitas pemerintahan, dan titik pertahanan-keamanan dengan kecepatan internet hingga 10 Mbps per lokasi.
Selain itu, Infrastruktur pendukung proyek SATRIA 1 dilengkapi dengan 11 gateway yang tersebar di Batam, Pontianak, Banjarmasin, Cikarang, Manado, Ambon, Kupang, Manokwari, Timika, Jayapura, dan Tarakan, yang berfungsi sebagai penghubung utama antara satelit dan jaringan  internet nasional.

snippet: Indonesia Bidik Basis Produksi Digital Asia Tenggara, Investasi AI dan Pusat Data Dibuka Batamtoday.com
article_text:

Cari artikel terbit. Mulai mengetik minimal dua karakter.
Penulis: Redaksi
BATAMTODAY.COM, Jakarta - Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Kemkomdigi) menargetkan Indonesia tidak lagi hanya menjadi pasar digital yang besar, tetapi berkembang menjadi basis produksi, inovasi, dan investasi digital di Asia Tenggara.
Wakil Menteri Komunikasi dan Digital (Wamen Komdigi) Nezar Patria, mengatakan arah tersebut didukung penguatan infrastruktur digital, pusat data, komputasi awan, pengembangan kecerdasan artifisial (AI), peningkatan kualitas talenta digital, serta kepastian regulasi bagi investor.
Pernyataan itu disampaikan Nezar dalam 14th US-Indonesia Investment Summit di Jakarta Selatan, Selasa (6/10/2026). “Indonesia siap beralih dari pasar digital besar menjadi basis produksi, inovasi, dan investasi digital utama di Asia Tenggara. Kami siap bekerja sama dengan perusahaan-perusahaan Amerika yang ingin membangun di sini untuk pasar Indonesia, untuk ASEAN, dan untuk kawasan Asia-Pasifik yang lebih luas,” ujar Nezar.
Menurut Nezar, Indonesia memiliki basis pengguna internet yang besar. Pada awal 2026, jumlah pengguna internet di Indonesia mencapai 235 juta orang atau sekitar 81,72 persen dari populasi. Di sisi infrastruktur, jaringan serat optik nasional telah mencapai sekitar 460.000 kilometer dan menjangkau lebih dari 5.000 kecamatan.
Namun, menurut Nezar, besarnya jumlah pengguna internet bukan satu-satunya faktor yang menjadi pertimbangan investor. Ketersediaan infrastruktur, kapasitas komputasi awan, keamanan arus data, talenta berkualitas, serta kepastian kebijakan menjadi faktor penting dalam membangun ekosistem digital.
“Investor tidak hanya mencari pengguna, tetapi juga infrastruktur, kapasitas cloud, aliran data yang aman, talenta berkualitas tinggi, dan kebijakan yang dapat diprediksi,” tuturnya.
Kemkomdigi terus memperkuat konektivitas nasional melalui berbagai infrastruktur, termasuk Palapa Ring dan SATRIA-1.
SATRIA-1 memiliki kapasitas 150 Gbps yang digunakan untuk mendukung sekitar 37.000 titik layanan publik. Infrastruktur tersebut juga dirancang untuk membantu memperluas akses konektivitas kepada hingga 45 juta masyarakat yang sebelumnya belum mendapatkan layanan internet secara memadai.
Sementara itu, hingga 2024, sebanyak 6.794 lokasi BTS telah beroperasi di wilayah perbatasan, terpencil, dan tertinggal.
Pemerintah juga menargetkan kecepatan mobile broadband mencapai 100 Mbps pada 2029. Target tersebut antara lain didukung optimalisasi spektrum pita menengah untuk pengembangan jaringan 5G.
Selain konektivitas, pemerintah membuka peluang investasi pada sektor pusat data, komputasi awan, kabel bawah laut, infrastruktur komputasi, dan energi terbarukan. “Dengan potensi pertumbuhan ekonomi digital Indonesia hingga lebih dari Rp 4.000 triliun pada 2029, pusat data, layanan cloud, sistem kabel bawah laut, komputasi, dan energi terbarukan merupakan peluang investasi strategis,” jelas Nezar.
Pemerintah juga menempatkan kecerdasan artifisial sebagai salah satu sektor strategis dalam transformasi digital nasional.
Kemkomdigi bersama lebih dari 30 kementerian dan lembaga menyusun Peta Jalan AI Nasional 2026–2029. Lima sektor menjadi prioritas utama, yakni kesehatan, pendidikan dan talenta digital, reformasi birokrasi, kota pintar, serta ketahanan pangan.
Pengembangan AI diarahkan dengan menekankan partisipasi pemangku kepentingan, inovasi, penguatan teknologi dan riset, serta mitigasi risiko.
Nezar menilai ekosistem AI yang dapat dipercaya tidak cukup hanya mengandalkan ketersediaan daya komputasi. Aspek akuntabilitas, keamanan, transparansi, tata kelola data, dan pengawasan manusia juga harus diperkuat.
“Ekosistem AI yang tepercaya membutuhkan lebih dari sekadar akses ke daya komputasi. Hal ini membutuhkan kejelasan mengenai akuntabilitas, keamanan, transparansi, tata kelola data, dan pengawasan manusia,” ungkapnya.
Kemkomdigi juga menyiapkan tata kelola pusat data nasional, cloud pemerintah, infrastruktur publik digital, serta peta jalan infrastruktur digital.
Pemerintah membuka ruang kolaborasi dengan perusahaan teknologi Amerika Serikat dalam berbagai bidang, mulai dari riset AI, penerapan AI yang bertanggung jawab, pengembangan solusi berbasis bahasa dan konteks lokal, infrastruktur AI, keamanan siber, hingga pengembangan talenta digital.
Sejumlah investasi perusahaan teknologi global telah menunjukkan minat terhadap pasar digital Indonesia.
Microsoft mengumumkan investasi US$ 1,7 miliar untuk pengembangan cloud dan AI di Indonesia. Investasi tersebut diproyeksikan memberikan dampak ekonomi sekitar US$ 2,5 miliar dan mendukung sekitar 60.000 lapangan kerja hingga 2028.
Sementara itu, AWS disebut telah menanamkan investasi sebesar US$ 5 miliar sejak 2021 dengan komitmen investasi hingga 2036. “Investasi ini tidak hanya membawa modal, tetapi juga kemampuan rekayasa, mitra lokal, kolaborasi penelitian, pengembangan tenaga kerja, dan layanan yang lebih baik bagi perusahaan-perusahaan di Indonesia,” kata Nezar.
Untuk memperkuat kepercayaan investor, pemerintah juga menyiapkan regulasi yang mendukung iklim investasi melalui konsultasi awal, panduan implementasi yang jelas, standar transparan, serta dialog publik dan swasta yang terstruktur.
Nezar menegaskan kepastian regulasi bukan berarti kebijakan tidak dapat berubah. Menurut dia, setiap perubahan harus disampaikan secara jelas, dikonsultasikan dengan pemangku kepentingan, dan diterapkan secara adil.
“Mari kita bangun kepercayaan itu melalui proyek-proyek konkret, hasil yang terukur, dan ekonomi digital yang terbuka terhadap inovasi, berlandaskan kepercayaan, dan inklusif dalam manfaatnya,” pungkas Nezar.

title: Komdigi: 812 Infrastruktur Telekomunikasi BTS di NTT Telah Pulih - investor.id
snippet: Komdigi: 812 Infrastruktur Telekomunikasi BTS di NTT Telah Pulih investor.id
article_text:
Jakarta, investor.id - Pemerintah melalui Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Komdigi) menyebut pemulihan infrastruktur telekomunikasi dalam hal ini Base Transceiver Station (BTS) di wilayah terdampak gempa Nusa Tenggara Timur, telah pulih 100%.
Direktur Jenderal Komunikasi Publik dan Media Komdigi, Fifi Aleyda Yahya mengungkapkan, berdasarkan identifikasi Komdigi, terdapat 812 site/BTS yang terdampak gempa saat bencana terjadi pada Sabtu (15/8/2026) lalu. Dan saat ini seluruh BTS yang tersebar di sejumlah kabupaten/kota di Provinsi NTT telah dipulihkan.
"Alhamdulillah sampai perhari ini laporannya terkait dengan konektivitas di wilayah terdampak gempa itu dari 812 titik atau site BTS. Alhamdulillah perhari ini sudah pulih 100 persen, yang terdampak di 8 kabupaten di NTT," ungkap Fifi Aleyda dalam penyerahan bantuan logistik secara simbolis di Kantor Badan Penghubung Nusa Tenggara Timur, Jakarta, Sabtu (22/6/2026).
Meskipun seluruh infrastruktur BTS telah berjalan normal, Komdigi tetap mengirimkan sejumlah bantuan untuk membantu masyarakat di wilayah terdampak bencana gempa bumi di NTT dan sekitarnya. Adapun salah satu bantuan yang diberikan yakni unit perangkat telekomunikasi Starlink.
Fifi menjelaskan pihaknya mengirimkan sekitar 20 unit perangkat. Adapun, bantuan perangkat tersebut diharapkan dapat membantu menjaga konektivitas di wilayah terdampak.
Menurutnya, ketersediaan dan penguatan konektivitas sangat penting untuk mempercepat koordinasi dan penanganan bencana. Dengan dukungan komunikasi yang memadai, petugas di lapangan diharapkan dapat lebih mudah berkoordinasi dalam menjalankan proses evakuasi, distribusi bantuan, maupun penanganan kebutuhan masyarakat terdampak.
Fifi mengatakan, bantuan tersebut merupakan bentuk kepedulian Komdigi terhadap masyarakat yang tengah menghadapi dampak gempa. Dia berharap bantuan logistik dan perangkat komunikasi yang diberikan dapat dimanfaatkan secara optimal untuk mendukung masyarakat maupun petugas di lapangan.
"Kalau untuk Starlink tentu tidak ada salahnya kami memberikan penguatan-penguatan jika masih ada titik-titik yang misalnya terdampak," pungkasnya.

title: Palapa Ring Tengah Masih Bermasalah, Satria-1 Dikerahkan - detikInet
snippet: Palapa Ring Tengah Masih Bermasalah, Satria-1 Dikerahkan detikInet
article_text:
Agus Tri Haryanto - detikInet
Jaringan fiber optik Palapa Ring Tengah segmen Tahuna-Melonguane masih alami gangguan, Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Komdigi) mengatasi layanan telekomunikasi dan internet masyarakat di sekitarnya menggunakan satelit Republik Indonesia (Satria-1).
Melalui Badang Aksesibilitas Telekomunikasi dan Informasi (Bakti), Komdigi menambah kapasitas bandwidth 50 Mbps sampai dengan 150 Mbps di 154 titik akses di Kabupaten Kepulauan Sangihe dan Kabupaten Kepulauan Siau Tagulandang Biaro (Sitaro) tetap terkoneksi.
Direktur Pengendalian Infrastruktur Digital Direktorat Jenderal Infrastruktur Digital Kementerian Komdigi Indra Maulana mengatakan pemerintah terus memprioritaskan keberlangsungan layanan bagi masyarakat sembari mengawal proses restorasi infrastruktur yang sedang berlangsung.
SCROLL TO CONTINUE WITH CONTENT
"Seluruh manuver operasional serta penggunaan peralatan bawah laut harus dilakukan secara sangat terukur. Kami harus berhati-hati untuk menjaga keamanan serta keandalan infrastruktur telekomunikasi eksisting di sekitar area kerja," ujar Indra Maulana dikutip siaran pers Rabu (3/6/2026).
Komdigi juga terus berkoordinasi dengan operator seluler guna memastikan konektivitas pada titik-titik layanan publik dan objek vital di wilayah tersebut tetap terjaga.
Upaya tersebut dilakukan untuk memastikan layanan komunikasi, layanan pemerintahan, pendidikan, kesehatan, dan aktivitas ekonomi masyarakat di wilayah perbatasan tetap terhubung.
Plt. Direktur Infrastruktur Bakti Darien Aldiano menyampaikan bahwa seluruh tim tetap bekerja maksimal untuk mempercepat proses pemulihan jaringan.
"Kami memohon maaf atas penyesuaian jadwal ini. Walau menghadapi tantangan cuaca dan karakteristik dasar laut yang ekstrem, seluruh tim teknis tetap berupaya maksimal. Pekerjaan terus dilaksanakan dengan mengedepankan aspek keselamatan dan keandalan jaringan agar layanan kembali normal secepatnya," tutur Darien Aldiano.
Disampaikan Komdigi bahwa pekerjaan restorasi jaringan Palapa Ring Tengah ini menghadapi sejumlah tantangan teknis di lapangan. Selain kondisi cuaca laut yang dinamis, area pekerjaan juga berada di dekat koridor kabel laut aktif segmen Ondong Siau-Tahuna sehingga seluruh proses harus dilakukan dengan tingkat presisi yang tinggi.
Tim teknis pun dihadapi kondisi dasar laut yang didominasi batuan dengan kontur yang curam. Situasi tersebut membuat proses identifikasi dan penanganan kabel memerlukan kehati-hatian lebih untuk menjaga keselamatan pekerjaan sekaligus memastikan kualitas hasil restorasi.
Dengan mempertimbangkan kondisi operasional tersebut, target penyelesaian pekerjaan dan jadwal Ready For Service (RFS) yang semula direncanakan pada periode 28 Mei hingga 2 Juni 2026 diproyeksikan disesuaikan hingga 6 Juni 2026.
Komdigi mengungkapkan komitmen terus mengawal proses restorasi hingga tuntas serta memastikan masyarakat di Sangihe dan Sitaro tetap mendapatkan akses komunikasi dan layanan digital yang andal sebagai bagian dari upaya menghadirkan konektivitas yang merata hingga wilayah perbatasan Indonesia.

title: Komdigi Bantah Kalah Cepat dari Starlink Pulihkan Internet di Lokasi Banjir Sumatra - Suara.com
snippet: Komdigi Bantah Kalah Cepat dari Starlink Pulihkan Internet di Lokasi Banjir Sumatra Suara.com
article_text:
Available On
Dicky Prastya
Suara.com - Badan Aksesibilitas Telekomunikasi dan Informasi Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital atau BAKTI Komdigi membantah kalau Pemerintah kalah cepat untuk memulihkan akses internet di wilayah terdampak banjir Sumatra .
Direktur Utama BAKTI Komdigi , Fadhilah Mathar mengklaim kalau Pemerintah melalui Kementerian Komdigi justru lebih cepat alih-alih kehadiran satelit Starlink milik Elon Musk yang banyak dipakai warga terdampak bencana Sumatra.
"Kita bukan terlambat, sebenarnya kita juga bahkan lebih cepat dibandingkan itu," katanya saat konferensi pers di Stasiun Bumi (Gateway) Satria-1 Satelit Nusantara Tiga, di Cikarang, Rabu (10/12/2025).
Perempuan yang akrab disapa Indah itu bercerita kalau BAKTI Komdigi sebelumnya justru lebih fokus memberikan akses konektivitas internet ketimbang sosialisasi terhadap program yang mereka lakukan.
Dicontohkan dia, BAKTI Komdigi sudah memulihkan 413 akses internet dari total 602 lokasi di wilayah Sumatra yang terdampak banjir per 6 Desember 2025.
Selain itu, BAKTI Komdigi juga menyediakan 18 titik lokasi untuk menyediakan akses internet darurat dari Satelit Republik Indonesia 1 atau Satria-1 di wilayah terdampak bencana Sumatra.
Menurut Indah, Satria 1 ini bisa menyediakan akses internet di seluruh Indonesia. Tak hanya untuk mengantisipasi blank spot karena bencana, satelit tersebut juga bisa menyediakan internet di wilayah 3T atau terdepan, terluar, tertinggal.
"Coverage-nya itu sudah melingkupi seluruh Indonesia sehingga bukan hanya kebencanaan ya, mungkin hal-hal lain yang memang memerlukan urgensi konektivitas, di wilayah-wilayah yang terestrial tidak mudah dijangkau," jelasnya.
Diketahui SATRIA-1 merupakan proyek Kerja Sama Pemerintah dan Badan Usaha (KPBU) yang menyediakan satelit berkapasitas 150 Gbps untuk memperkuat konektivitas digital, khususnya di wilayah tertinggal, terdepan, terluar (3T), serta lokasi prioritas layanan publik yang beroperasi sejak tahun 2024.
Baca Juga
Dengan total investasi sekitar Rp 6,42 triliun dan skema Build–Operate–Transfer (BOT), proyek ini dilaksanakan oleh PT Satelit Nusantara Tiga (SNT) sebagai Badan Usaha Pelaksana (BUP), dengan Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Komdigi) selaku Penanggung Jawab Proyek Kerja Sama (PJPK), di mana sebagian wewenangnya didelegasikan kepada BAKTI Komdigi.
Hingga 7 Desember 2025, SATRIA-1 telah menghubungkan 30.017 titik layanan publik di seluruh Indonesia, termasuk sekolah, puskesmas, fasilitas pemerintahan, dan titik pertahanan-keamanan dengan kecepatan internet hingga 10 Mbps per lokasi.
Selain itu, Infrastruktur pendukung proyek SATRIA 1 dilengkapi dengan 11 gateway yang tersebar di Batam, Pontianak, Banjarmasin, Cikarang, Manado, Ambon, Kupang, Manokwari, Timika, Jayapura, dan Tarakan, yang berfungsi sebagai penghubung utama antara satelit dan jaringan  internet nasional.

title: Bakti Tegaskan Tak Ada Pembangunan BTS Baru di Tahun Ini - InvestorTrust
snippet: Bakti Tegaskan Tak Ada Pembangunan BTS Baru di Tahun Ini InvestorTrust
article_text:
JAKARTA, Investortrust.id - Badan Aksesibilitas Telekomunikasi dan Informasi (Bakti) Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Kemenkomdigi) mengubah fokus pengelolaan infrastruktur telekomunikasi pada 2026. Bakti menyebut tidak akan membangun menara telekomunikasi ( base transceiver station /BTS) baru.
Direktur Utama Bakti Kemenkomdigi, Fadhilah Mathar mengatakan, fokus tersebut mencakup pengelolaan sekitar 6.747 BTS yang sudah beroperasi. Infrastruktur itu terutama menopang konektivitas di wilayah 3T yang belum menjadi prioritas jaringan komersial.
“Di 2026 ini kita tidak ada pembangunan BTS baru. Kita fokus kepada opex dan maintenance ,” kata wanita yang akrab disapa Indah itu dalam Bakti Media Connect 2026 di Jakarta, Rabu (12/8/2026).
Perkuat Strategi Penurunan Emisi, Telkomsel (TSEL) Operasikan 1.361 BTS Tenaga Surya
Menurutnya, biaya operasional menjadi komponen penting untuk memastikan aset yang telah dibangun tetap memberikan layanan. Bakti juga melakukan evaluasi terhadap kualitas dan pemanfaatan jaringan di berbagai lokasi. “Jadi bagaimana existing infrastructure ini bisa memberikan layanan yang optimal,” ujarnya.
Evaluasi dilakukan agar investasi pemerintah tidak berhenti pada pembangunan fisik, tetapi menghasilkan layanan yang benar-benar digunakan masyarakat. Optimalisasi juga dilakukan melalui relokasi BTS apabila terdapat lokasi yang dinilai kurang efektif.
Selain BTS, Bakti juga mendorong pemanfaatan infrastruktur satelit untuk meningkatkan kapasitas layanan. Migrasi sejumlah titik ke SATRIA-1 menjadi salah satu opsi untuk mengatasi keterbatasan kapasitas di lokasi tertentu.
BTS Sulit Jangkau Wilayah 3T, Kemenkomdigi Dorong Satelit LEO Jadi Solusi Daerah 'Blank Spot'
Indah mengatakan efisiensi menjadi pertimbangan utama dalam pengelolaan infrastruktur Bakti. “Kita harus melihat mana yang memang masih membutuhkan intervensi pemerintah dan mana yang sudah bisa berjalan secara komersial,” jelasnya.
Fokus Bakti pada tahun ini pun 2026 tak lagi mengejar jumlah BTS baru. "Prioritasnya adalah menjaga jaringan existing , meningkatkan kualitas layanan, melakukan optimalisasi aset, dan memastikan belanja infrastruktur digital memberikan dampak maksimal bagi masyarakat 3T," tutup Indah.

title: Duh! Komdigi Ungkap 2.121 Desa Blankspot Belum Teraliri Internet - detikFinance
snippet: Duh! Komdigi Ungkap 2.121 Desa Blankspot Belum Teraliri Internet detikFinance
article_text:
Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Komdigi) mengungkapkan sebanyak 2.121 desa di wilayah tertinggal, terdepan dan terluar (3T) belum teraliri internet. Itu artinya wilayah tersebut belum memiliki akses komunikasi dan informasi digital.
"Ada sekitar 2.121 desa yang masih blankspot, artinya 0% coverage selular 4G," kata Direktur Utama Badan Aksesibilitas Telekomunikasi dan Informasi (Bakti) Komdigi Fadhilah Mathar di Stasiun Bumi Satelit SATRIA-1, Cikarang, Jawa Barat, Rabu (10/12/205).
Fadhilah menyebut pihaknya berkomitmen untuk menghadirkan internet merata hingga ke pelosok Indonesia. Meski demikian, jenis teknologinya akan disesuaikan setiap desa tergantung jumlah penduduknya.
SCROLL TO CONTINUE WITH CONTENT
"Selain desktop analisis, kami juga lihat berdasarkan pantauan satelit, itu tidak semua desa ini berpenghuni atau berpemukiman sehingga ini nanti akan berpengaruh kepada pemilihan teknologi," ucapnya.
"Misalnya dalam satu desa itu jumlah penduduknya tidak terlalu banyak dan mereka tersentralisasi di suatu tempat, tidak harus teknologinya teknologi seluler, kita bisa memberikan misalnya super wifi karena masih bisa mencakup jumlah penduduk di desa tersebut," tambahnya.
Dari proyek Satelit Multifungsi Pemerintah (SATRIA-1), sampai 7 Desember 2025 pemerintah telah menghubungkan 30.017 titik layanan publik di seluruh Indonesia termasuk sekolah, Puskesmas, fasilitas pemerintahan dan titik pertahanan-keamanan dengan kecepatan internet up to 10 Mbps/lokasi.
Selain itu, Infrastruktur pendukung proyek SATRIA-1 dilengkapi dengan 11 gateway yang tersebar di Batam, Pontianak, Banjarmasin, Cikarang, Manado, Ambon, Kupang, Manokwari, Timika, Jayapura dan Tarakan yang berfungsi sebagai penghubung utama antara satelit dan jaringan internet nasional.
Sebagai informasi, SATRIA-1 merupakan proyek kerja sama pemerintah dan badan usaha (KPBU) yang menyediakan satelit berkapasitas 150 Gbps untuk memperkuat konektivitas digital, khususnya di wilayah 3T serta lokasi prioritas layanan publik.
Dengan total investasi sekitar Rp 6,42 triliun dan skema Build-Operate Transfer (BOT), proyek ini dilaksanakan oleh PT Satelit Nusantara Tiga (SNT) sebagai Badan Usaha Pelaksana (BUP) dan Komdigi selaku Penanggung Jawab Proyek Kerja Sama (PJPK).
Penjaminan turut diberikan oleh PT Penjaminan Infrastruktur Indonesia (Persero) atau PII sebagai faktor kunci dalam mendorong keberhasilan proyek SATRIA-1 mendapatkan dukungan pembiayaan.
"Lewat dukungan yang kami berikan dalam memberikan penjaminan pemerintah serta capacity building terkait proyek KPBU Satria-1 ini, kami berharap dapat memberikan dampak optimal bagi seluruh pemangku kepentingan," tutur Plt Direktur Utama PT PII Andre Permana.

title: Sinyal Darurat Dikebut, Satria & Starlink Dikerahkan Pulihkan Internet Sumatera - detikInet
snippet: Sinyal Darurat Dikebut, Satria & Starlink Dikerahkan Pulihkan Internet Sumatera detikInet
article_text:
Adi Fida Rahman - detikInet
Guna mempercepat pemulihan akses telekomunikasi yang terdampak banjir bandang di sejumlah wilayah Sumatera, pemerintah bersama operator menambah layanan berbasis satelit untuk memastikan konektivitas di lokasi bencana tetap tersedia.
Direktur Utama Bakti Komdigi, Fadhilah Mathar, memaparkan bahwa pihaknya telah menambah titik akses internet di Aceh, Sumatera Utara (Sumut), dan Sumatera Barat (Sumbar) menjadi 14 lokasi dari sebelumnya 10 titik.
"Hari ini kita sudah menyediakan sampai 14 lokasi. Memang ada lokasi yang belum bisa kita tempuh karena ada jalan yang putus. Alhamdulillah, kita dibantu oleh Basarnas, TNI, dan BNPB bisa memobilisasi ke lokasi-lokasi tersebut yang sangat membantu kami penyediaan backup akses internet," ujar Fadhilah di Balai Monitoring Komdigi Medan, Senin (1/12/2025).
SCROLL TO CONTINUE WITH CONTENT
Layanan internet berbasis satelit Starlink milik SpaceX juga turut membantu penyediaan konektivitas kepada pemerintah dengan memberikan 32 unit perangkat, termasuk dukungan genset untuk menghidupkan perangkat tersebut di lapangan.
"Dan sekarang sudah mulai on air di beberapa tempat, termasuk misalnya di Tapanuli Tengah, antara lain di SMA dan juga posko-posko BNPB," ucapnya.
Ia menambahkan, kebutuhan titik baru masih terus berkembang. "Selain itu, kami harapkan apabila nanti di lokasi-lokasi penambahan baru karena per hari ini usulan dari BNPB, Pemda, maupun Kemendagri itu 139 lokasi. Nanti setelah ini kita koordinasi kembali untuk penyediaan backup berupa WiFi di lokasi-lokasi tersebut," tutur perempuan yang disapa Indah ini.
Pada kesempatan yang sama, Direktur Jenderal Infrastruktur Digital Komdigi, Wayan Toni Supriyanto, menjelaskan bahwa pengerahan akses internet satelit menjadi langkah kolaboratif untuk menjaga akses telekomunikasi di tengah belum pulihnya infrastruktur darat.
"Memang saat ini kita sangat mengandalkan Satria dan Starlink ya untuk memenuhi kebutuhan emergensi dalam masa kritis ini, artinya di mana dalam persiapan untuk recovery keseluruhannya," pungkas Wayan.
Diberitakan sebelumnya, Menteri Komunikasi dan Digital (Menkomdigi) Meutya Hafid memimpin rapat koordinasi penanganan akses telekomunikasi di Aceh, Sumut, dan Sumbar.
Berdasarkan pantau detikINET yang berada di lokasi ada pimpinan penyelenggara telekomunikasi, yakni Direktur Utama Telkom Dian Siswarini, Direktur Utama Telkomsel Nugroho, Chief Technology Officer Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison Desmond Cheung, Director & Chief Regulatory Officer XLSmart Merza Fachys, dan Market Access Manager Starlink Indonesia Tommy Des Mulianta.

title: SATRIA-1 Jadi Tulang Punggung Internet di Wilayah Terluar Indonesia - BeritaSatu.com
snippet: SATRIA-1 Jadi Tulang Punggung Internet di Wilayah Terluar Indonesia BeritaSatu.com
article_text:
Jakarta,  Beritasatu.com - Sebanyak 30.017 titik layanan publik di Indonesia telah terhubung internet melalui Satelit SATRIA-1 hingga awal Desember 2025. Jangkauan ini mencakup wilayah terdepan, terluar, dan tertinggal (3T), sekaligus menjadi tulang punggung penyediaan akses internet cepat di daerah yang sebelumnya sulit dijangkau infrastruktur darat.
BACA JUGA
Dari total tersebut, sektor pendidikan mendominasi dengan 20.785 lokasi atau 69,24 persen, disusul 5.846 kantor pemerintahan (19,48 persen), 1.689 fasilitas kesehatan (5,63 persen), serta 1.697 titik lainnya seperti pusat internet komunitas di pedesaan. SATRIA-1 memiliki kapasitas hingga 150 Gbps dengan kecepatan layanan internet mencapai 10 Mbps, dan telah beroperasi sejak 2024 di bawah pengelolaan Badan Aksesibilitas Telekomunikasi dan Informasi (BAKTI) Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital.
BACA JUGA
Melalui sistem pemancaran sinyal satelit yang diteruskan ke stasiun bumi dan perangkat VSAT di lokasi layanan, SATRIA-1 berperan dalam pemerataan akses informasi, mempersempit kesenjangan digital antara kota besar dan wilayah terpencil, serta menjaga konektivitas saat infrastruktur darat terganggu, terutama dalam kondisi bencana. Kehadiran satelit ini diharapkan memperkuat layanan pendidikan, kesehatan, dan pemerintahan sekaligus mendorong percepatan transformasi digital yang inklusif di seluruh Indonesia.

title: Kominfo Hadirkan 10 Titik Internet Satria-1 untuk Dukung Komunikasi di Area Banjir Sumater - KUYOU.ID
snippet: Kominfo Hadirkan 10 Titik Internet Satria-1 untuk Dukung Komunikasi di Area Banjir Sumater KUYOU.ID
article_text:
Kementerian Komunikasi dan Informatika (Kominfo) memasang 10 titik internet berbasis satelit Satria-1 di wilayah terdampak banjir bandang di Sumatera. Fasilitas ini diprioritaskan untuk mendukung kebutuhan komunikasi darurat dan koordinasi penanganan bencana di lapangan.
Pemasangan akses internet dilakukan di sejumlah area yang mengalami kerusakan jaringan akibat bencana. Dengan hadirnya layanan Satria-1, tim gabungan, relawan, hingga masyarakat dapat kembali berkomunikasi untuk melaporkan kondisi, mengakses informasi bantuan, serta mempercepat proses evakuasi.
Kominfo menyebut bahwa pemulihan konektivitas merupakan salah satu langkah penting untuk mempercepat distribusi logistik dan kebutuhan dasar korban banjir. Dukungan jaringan ini juga diharapkan membantu pemerintah daerah dalam memperbarui data situasi secara real time.
Selain memasang akses internet satelit, Kominfo juga berkoordinasi dengan operator seluler untuk memperbaiki infrastruktur telekomunikasi yang rusak akibat banjir bandang. Perbaikan jaringan diupayakan dilakukan secara bertahap sesuai kondisi lapangan.
Keberadaan layanan komunikasi darurat menjadi penopang penting dalam masa krisis, terlebih ketika warga dan aparat membutuhkan akses cepat untuk penanganan medis, informasi pengungsian, dan pemulihan pasca-bencana

TRIBUNSUMSEL.COM -- Tahun 2026 menjadi tonggak bersejarah bagi Indonesia. Tepat 50 tahun lalu, pada 8 Juli 1976, Satelit Palapa A1 meluncur dari Cape Canaveral, Amerika Serikat, menandai dimulainya era komunikasi satelit nasional.
Sejak saat itu, perjalanan teknologi satelit Indonesia terus berkembang, mulai dari keluarga Satelit Palapa, Telkom, BRIsat, Nusantara Satu, hingga SATRIA-1. Selama lima dekade, satelit telah menjadi tulang punggung komunikasi nasional, penyiaran televisi, layanan perbankan, internet, pendidikan, kesehatan, hingga pertahanan negara.
Di era transformasi digital, keberadaan satelit selain sebagai infrastruktur telekomunikasi, juga bagian penting dari upaya menjaga kedaulatan digital Indonesia dari ruang angkasa.
Artikel ini menguraikan secara singkat perjalanan satelit Indonesia melayani konektivitas yang semakin maju
Peluncuran Palapa A1 pada 8 Juli 1976 merupakan salah satu pencapaian teknologi terbesar Indonesia pada abad ke-20. Satelit ini diluncurkan menggunakan roket Delta dari Cape Canaveral, Florida, Amerika Serikat.
Saat itu Indonesia menjadi negara ketiga di dunia, setelah Amerika Serikat dan Kanada, yang memiliki Domestic Satellite Communication System (DSCS) atau sistem satelit komunikasi domestik.
Nama Palapa diambil dari Sumpah Palapa Mahapatih Gajah Mada, yang melambangkan tekad mempersatukan Nusantara. Filosofi tersebut diwujudkan melalui satelit yang menghubungkan ribuan pulau Indonesia dalam satu jaringan komunikasi.
Sebelum Palapa hadir, komunikasi antarpulau berlangsung lambat dan mahal. Jaringan telepon masih terbatas, sementara siaran televisi belum menjangkau seluruh Indonesia.
Melalui Palapa, masyarakat di Aceh, Papua, Kalimantan, Sulawesi hingga Nusa Tenggara dapat menikmati siaran televisi nasional secara bersamaan. Layanan telepon jarak jauh menjadi lebih cepat, komunikasi pemerintahan semakin efektif, dan pembangunan nasional memperoleh dukungan infrastruktur komunikasi yang lebih baik.
Tak heran bila Satelit Palapa sering disebut sebagai simbol pemersatu Indonesia modern.
Dikutip dari laman komdigi.go.id, berikut perjalanan satelit Indonesia selama 50 tahun atau usia emas, mulai dari Generasi Palapa hingga SATRIA, Indonesia terus memperkuat armada satelitnya.

Masing-masing generasi membawa peningkatan kapasitas transponder, jangkauan layanan, serta kualitas komunikasi untuk memenuhi kebutuhan masyarakat yang terus berkembang.
Memasuki era internet, PT Telkom Indonesia mengembangkan armada satelit sendiri.

title: Perkuat Konektivitas Digital, Surveyor Indonesia Jaga Kualitas Jaringan Selama Mudik Lebaran 2026 - Liputan6.com
snippet: Perkuat Konektivitas Digital, Surveyor Indonesia Jaga Kualitas Jaringan Selama Mudik Lebaran 2026 Liputan6.com
article_text:
Keandalan satelit SATRIA-1 memungkinkan masyarakat tetap terhubung dengan layanan publik esensial meskipun berada di jalur mudik yang padat.
Liputan6.com, Jakarta - PT Surveyor Indonesia mempertegas perannya dalam menjaga kelancaran arus Mudik Lebaran 2026 dengan memberikan pengawasan ketat pada sektor infrastruktur digital.
Sebagai bagian dari layanan assurance dan verifikasi independen, perusahaan pelat merah ini fokus memastikan jaringan telekomunikasi nasional tetap stabil dan andal guna mendukung komunikasi serta akses informasi masyarakat selama perjalanan ke kampung halaman.
Direktur Utama PT Surveyor Indonesia, Fajar Wibhiyadi, menegaskan bahwa peran perusahaan sebagai Guardian of Assurance menjadi krusial dalam menjaga ritme mobilitas masyarakat yang masif.
Advertisement
“Momentum mudik Lebaran merupakan salah satu mobilitas masyarakat terbesar di Indonesia. Oleh karena itu, kami berkomitmen memastikan berbagai infrastruktur dan layanan publik yang digunakan masyarakat--mulai dari transportasi, konektivitas digital, hingga jaminan produk halal--memenuhi standar kualitas, keamanan, dan keandalan,” ujar Fajar dalam keterangannya, Rabu (18/3/2026).
Dalam aspek infrastruktur digital, Surveyor Indonesia mengawal operasional Satelit SATRIA-1 yang menjadi tulang punggung akses internet di wilayah-wilayah strategis. Pengawasan ini memastikan konektivitas tetap terjaga di 30.017 titik layanan publik di seluruh Indonesia.
Cakupan ini meliputi fasilitas kesehatan hingga kantor layanan pemerintah daerah yang menjadi titik krusial selama masa libur panjang.
Keandalan satelit ini memungkinkan masyarakat tetap terhubung dengan layanan publik esensial meskipun berada di daerah terpencil atau jalur mudik yang padat.
Dengan ketersediaan bandwidth yang terjaga, arus data dan informasi terkait navigasi mudik serta koordinasi tanggap darurat dapat berjalan tanpa kendala teknis berarti.
Selain fokus pada telekomunikasi, Surveyor Indonesia juga menjalankan fungsi verifikasi pada sektor transportasi untuk menjamin keamanan fisik pemudik.
Di sektor perkeretaapian, perusahaan memastikan kelaikan 10 trainset gerbong New Generation yang beroperasi di sepanjang Pulau Jawa.
Di tingkat mobilitas perkotaan, layanan Buy The Service (BTS) di 10 kota besar Indonesia juga terus dipantau untuk memastikan standar layanan bus kota tetap prima.
Tidak hanya transportasi massal, keamanan kendaraan pribadi pun tak luput dari pengawasan. Surveyor Indonesia melakukan inspeksi independen terhadap proses produksi kendaraan bermotor, termasuk kendaraan listrik dan Low Cost Green Car (LCGC), guna menjamin standar keselamatan pemudik yang menggunakan jalur darat.
Advertisement
Melengkapi kesiapan infrastruktur, Surveyor Indonesia sebagai Lembaga Pemeriksa Halal Utama turut memastikan aspek konsumsi masyarakat.
Hingga saat ini, sebanyak 4.575 pelaku usaha telah melalui proses pemeriksaan halal, memberikan ketenangan bagi masyarakat dalam menikmati hidangan Idulfitri di berbagai daerah.
Melalui pendekatan assurance yang komprehensif, perusahaan berupaya meminimalisir risiko gangguan teknis, baik di jalur transportasi maupun di jaringan siber. Langkah ini diharapkan mampu memberikan rasa aman dan nyaman bagi jutaan pemudik dalam merayakan momen kemenangan di kampung halaman.

title: Indonesia’s digital direction under Prabowo - The Strategist | ASPI's analysis and commentary site
snippet: Indonesia’s digital direction under Prabowo The Strategist | ASPI's analysis and commentary site
source: The Strategist | ASPI's analysis and commentary site
article_text:
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s first year in office has made clear that his technology agenda is about digital sovereignty and state capacity, beyond shiny infrastructure. While his digital policy sits quietly behind populist social programs of free nutritious meals for students and healthcare vouchers for the poor, it’s no less impactful. The jury is still out on how effective his digital policy is in supporting Indonesia’s ambitious 8 percent economic growth target, but it marks a distinct shift from his predecessor’s focus on infrastructure development.
Where previous president Joko Widodo’s time prioritised physical expansion, Prabowo is systematising the digital stack by integrating data , cybersecurity and AI governance . Beyond building national data centres to add capacity and consolidate digital systems, Prabowo’s administration will also pursue a multifunctional satellite system to integrate the Palapa Ring—a project that aims to provide nationwide 4G internet access—and the Satria-1 satellite, connecting all fibreoptic networks across the country.
The administration is pursuing a National Single Socioeconomic Data framework, which would merge social and economic registries to reduce duplication in providing government services. This sits on a broader Digital Public Infrastructure program, branded Digital Nusantara , aimed at enabling secure data exchange across ministries. The program, supported by the United Nations Development Programme, will first unify social protection systems before expanding to digital civil registration, health services and payment systems.
On AI, the approach is pragmatic, moving beyond soft ethics guidance towards practical implementation. Presidential Regulation 83/2025, issued in August, provides a directive for AI use in public services. It aims to improve bureaucratic efficiency by 400 trillion Indonesian rupiah (around $40 billion AUD) to ease the fiscal deficit. Yet, Prabowo is aware of AI risks. He has warned of misinformation, pointing to deepfake videos of him speaking Mandarin and Arabic as examples.
The social aspects of cybersecurity underpin much of Prabowo’s digital policy. The government has established a digital-space supervision unit within the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs and a cyber team to combat disinformation surrounding government programs. Officials argue that such monitoring is essential to protect citizens from online risks, including human trafficking, child exploitation and online gambling, even as civil-society groups warn the increased surveillance may breach human rights. But reality on the ground factors more into Jakarta’s caution, with hundreds of Indonesians trafficked to Cambodia , Myanmar and the Philippines and forced to work in scam centres.
Internationally, Indonesia is becoming a proactive digital actor. Prabowo has positioned AI as a tool for development by linking digitalisation efforts to its partnership with the United States through the International Technology Security and Innovation Fund. He also included data transfer components when negotiating a reduction in US tariffs from 32 to 19 percent. Insider accounts also suggest that Indonesia is working on a cybersecurity partnership with Britain following Prabowo’s November 2024 meeting with Prime Minister Keir Starmer.
Domestically, the government is drafting a roadmap for AI, semiconductors, and the broader tech ecosystem to meet global standards while empowering local innovation efforts, such as the Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard ( QRIS ) that supports the digitalisation of small and medium enterprises.
For Australia, Indonesia’s evolving digital landscape offers both opportunities and challenges. With digital economy contributing 19 percent of Indonesia’s GDP, Canberra should see Jakarta as a tech collaborator. The alignment is natural, as Australia’s Southeast Asia Economic Strategy to 2040 identifies the digital economy as a key growth driver, while Indonesia seeks reliable partners to enhance cybersecurity, AI governance and digital-skills development.
There is potential for collaboration in joint capability-building and innovation. Australia’s government economic development program Prospera is a promising starting point for deepening ties, as is private sector collaboration offered by Trellis Data to build large language models in Yogyakarta.
Both countries could exchange learning on AI-for-productivity pilots and training in critical infrastructure protection and incident response. Additionally, policy and technical fellowships that Australia has been providing for Indonesia since the 2010s can be geared towards joint products, papers and briefings to build cyber-resilience and digital-infrastructure interoperability.
To accelerate this, Jakarta should streamline its policies for permits so the two countries can co-innovate. For example, the Australia-Asia PowerLink project, also known as SunCable, would benefit from such streamlining. The project aims to facilitate transport of 1.75 gigawatts of electricity through Indonesia’s territorial waters. But since its 2021 signing , it has faced delays in processing of permits due to a lack of visible benefit for Indonesia. However, the September establishment of the SunCable Tech Research Park in the Riau Islands marked a step towards collaborative work on renewable energy and digital technologies. Expanding such joint innovation platforms could yield mutual gains.
Under Prabowo, development and digitalisation are intertwined. For Australia, engaging with Indonesia is less about exporting governance models and more about co-creating cyber norms and capacities for the next phase of digital transformation. If successful, Australia–Indonesia digital collaboration could be the new cornerstones of practical middle-power diplomacy.
Fitriani is a senior analyst at ASPI and Jascha Ramba Santoso is a Strategic Studies Masters Student at the Australian National University and a research intern at ASPI.

title: Exclusive, BAKTI Komdigi Virgie Baker Supervisory Board: Ensure Internet Network in Remote Areas - VOI.ID
snippet: Exclusive, BAKTI Komdigi Virgie Baker Supervisory Board: Ensure Internet Network in Remote Areas VOI.ID
article_text:
Share:
The vast natural conditions and diverse topography make development in Indonesia a major challenge. The same is true in the field of communication and information. In this condition, according to the BAKTI Komdigi Supervisory Board, Virgie Baker, SS, MSI, the government is present. However, the role that has been and continues to be carried out is not satisfactory to all parties because of various obstacles here and there.
***
The role as a Supervisory Board took him back on a long journey to various regions, including the 3T area. From the city center, the journey still has to continue for hours through land and sea routes to reach the points of connectivity services.
There, Virgie Baker didn't just look at the numbers in the report. He wanted to make sure for himself whether the network really arrived, whether the community could use it, and what the connectivity was used for.
Experience as a journalist makes him accustomed to checking and rechecking. For him, reports are still important, but the voice of the community as a beneficiary is no less important. "I can't just accept the report. There must be a check and recheck."
This point of view is important when BAKTI Komdigi carries out various strategic projects to expand Indonesia's connectivity, including through BTS and SATRIA-1 Satellites.
For Virgie, the success of development does not stop when the infrastructure has been built or the network has been available. The size is actually seen after that: do people really get the benefits?
Because, a BTS can be built. Satellites can provide connectivity. However, if the community is not able to use it optimally, the work is not completely finished.
"The measure of success is not only how much infrastructure is built, but whether the infrastructure is actually used and provides benefits for the community," he told Edy Suherli, Bambang Eros, and Ahmad Taufik from VOI in Tanah Abang, Central Jakarta, September 21, 2026.
What is the condition like after the legal case at Bakti Komdigi is complete and you join the Supervisory Board?
"Now the important lesson is that the development of infrastructure, whether small or large, must always go hand in hand with strong governance. Therefore, in every decision-making, we always first see what the check and balance is like. The risks must also be opened transparently, discussed together, then decided. So everything must be clear and measurable. As a Supervisory Board, we are also not just looking for mistakes. There is an assumption that the Supervisory Board's task is to find, "Where is this wrong?" Although it is not like that.
At BAKTI, we routinely ask management to be transparent to us. After that, we together look at and assess each decision. Most importantly, every decision must have a strong foundation and provide benefits for the community. So, everything must have a clear foundation.
"What other governance changes after the big incident?"
Actually, it doesn't mean that the management system has changed. What is more important is to ensure that the existing management system is actually carried out. SOP is already there, regulations are also there. But the challenge is how all of that becomes a work culture.
Regulations can be made as much as possible. However, when the leader does not set an example, in the end the rules will not become the maximum work culture and will not become a pattern in daily life in a corporation. Therefore, transparency, accountability, and supervision must really become a culture at BAKTI Komdigi.
"As the Supervisory Board, what else can be done?
"As the Supervisory Board, we do not get into daily operations. We do not even participate in drafting the organizational structure down to the lowest level. Our task is more to ensure that everything goes as it should. We also alternately monitor and evaluate to various regions. It just so happens that I was a journalist. So, when it comes to a certain point, I can't just accept the report. There must be check and recheck.
"I usually go down directly, go around and ask the community: can this network be used or not? Is it up or not? What is it used for? From there, sometimes we find that conditions in the field are not always exactly as written in the report.
"I then bring the findings back to the meeting. So, we also have to always listen to input. The process is not only about ensuring transparency, accountability, and compliance. We also have to hear the voices of beneficiaries.
Why is the voice of the community as the beneficiary important in supervision?
Because in the end the beneficiaries are the people. We have to see how the community receives everything we have built. The budget is large and the project is strategic. But if in the end the community does not get the benefits, it will certainly be something that is wasteful.
For example, many BTS have been built and internet access is available. But if the community turns out not to be able to use it, the problem is not just the network that is smooth or not. There are other problems, namely how the community uses it. That's where digital literacy is important. Don't let the technology that we have prepared and have reached the community finally does not provide maximum benefits. Not only because they don't know how to use it, but also because they don't have the right ethics in using technology.
That's the most important thing. Don't let technology be misused. So, one of the tasks of the Supervisory Board is to ensure that the benefits do not stop at infrastructure development, but actually reach the community.
"The last area visited to carry out monitoring where?
"The last time I went to Papua, specifically a few days ago to Manokwari.
Is it only in Manokwari City or up to the hinterland?
It goes to the hinterland. From the city, we still have to travel about three hours by land and two hours by sea. It's far, but it's exactly what's interesting. If you were a journalist, the further the area you have to visit, the more challenging it is.
Moreover, the areas we visited are in the 3T area or the outermost area. So don't expect that after arriving at the airport, the destination point is finished. For example, we go to Kupang, East Nusa Tenggara. The city of Kupang itself is not a 3T area. It is a big city and the provincial capital.
"We have to go back to the district, for example, Kupang Regency. From the district capital, there is still a journey of several hours to the BTS point which is the destination. There is also Rote which is one of the southernmost areas. So it's a challenge like that.
BAKTI has Satria-1 Satellite which is one of the strategic projects. How important is this satellite for Indonesian connectivity?
Satria-1 is indeed a strategic project because Indonesia's geographical conditions do not allow all regions to get connectivity services in the same way. There are areas that can be served with BTS, microwave, or fiber optic. But for remote islands, satellites are one of the most feasible technologies to reach those areas. Satria-1 has a capacity of 150 Gbps, with 116 spot beams and 11 gateways.
"It sounds technical, but basically this infrastructure is used to support various public services, such as health, education, government offices, as well as defense and security, especially in the 3T areas. In these areas, economically, the commercial value is often small. Therefore, business actors are not necessarily interested in entering. That's where the government must be present.
What are the examples of the benefits of connectivity for people in the 3T area?
For example, it can be seen from health services. In the past, when a health center in the 3T area needed a drug that was not available in the area, they had to send letters in a tiered manner. From the village, district, regency or city, province, to Jakarta. Imagine how long the process is. Meanwhile, the patient needs the drug immediately.
Now, after connectivity is available in the area, the process is much faster. They can immediately send information digitally and communicate with the parties needed. This means that connectivity is not just about the internet. There are public services that become much faster because of access to communication.
Does that mean BTS and satellites like Satria-1 complement each other?
Yes, that's right. The two complement each other.
For the coverage of Satria-1 itself, is it all of Indonesia or only certain areas?
In terms of coverage, Satria-1 can reach all of Indonesia. However, the focus is indeed on areas that need it, especially the 3T areas. So we determine the spot beam according to the needs of the area to be served.
If compared to Elon Musk's Starlink, is the technology similar?
Different. Starlink uses low orbit satellites, while Satria-1 is in a much higher orbit. Because it is in a different orbit, its characteristics and technology are also different. Low orbit satellites are relatively lower so they have their own characteristics in providing services.
So it's not right to just compare. Each has its own technology and allocation. The important thing is, Satria-1 can complement BTS-BTS that are not yet available in certain areas. Currently, Satria-1 has around 31,864 connected service points, with a number of users reaching around 1.4 million.
For people who use Satria-1 services, are they charged?
No. The beneficiary community is not charged.
From field observation, what is the condition of the use of Satria-1, especially in terms of signal smoothness and its utilization by the community?
Until now, there are certain areas that in certain conditions experience disturbances, especially when the weather is not good. But in general, more people feel the benefits. That is what we are most grateful for. The infrastructure that was built finally really benefits the community, especially those in the 3T area.
Because in the end, the measure of success is not only how much infrastructure is built, but whether the infrastructure is actually used and provides benefits for the community.
If you look at the benefits felt by the community, especially in the 3T area, what is the most memorable experience in the field for you?
The most memorable thing is when we see for ourselves how connectivity changes people's lives. Sometimes we see the numbers in the report. How many BTS have been built, how many points have been connected, how many users. But when we come directly to the field and meet the people, we can see that behind the numbers there is a life that has really changed.
For example, when a health center in the 3T area can now communicate faster with other regions. Previously, to get medicine or convey certain needs, the process could be very long because it had to go through letters in stages.
Now, with connectivity, communication can be done much faster. For us it may seem simple. Just send a message or communicate online. But for people in areas that were previously difficult to access, it can be a very meaningful change.
"This means for you, the measure of the success of connectivity development is not just how much infrastructure is built?
"True. Infrastructure is important, but what is much more important is the benefits. Don't let us feel that we have succeeded just because the BTS is standing or the network is available. We have to see if people can really use it.
Therefore, when I go to the field, I always want to see it directly. Does the signal arrive? Can the community use it? What is it used for? And do they understand how to use it well? So, the development of connectivity is not just about presenting technology. We also have to ensure that the community is ready to use the technology.
That's where digital literacy becomes important, right?
Yes, it is very important. Don't let the technology be available, but the public doesn't understand how to use it. Especially if the technology is used without ethics. We certainly want the internet to be something that provides benefits. Can help education, health, government services, economy, and various community needs. Therefore, in addition to building the infrastructure, we must also build the human resources.
What do you usually feel when you go directly to remote areas and see the conditions of the people there?
There is a sense of challenge, but also a sense of gratitude. Because if you only look at the report, you may not really understand what the conditions of the people in the area are like. When we come directly, we travel for hours by land, then continue the sea journey, we really feel how the geographical challenges of Indonesia are.
And it is precisely from there that we understand more about why the government must be present. Not all areas can be calculated based on their economic value. There are areas that may not be commercially attractive to companies, but the people there still have the same right to access communication and information.
So, the trip to the 3T area also changed the way of looking at digital development?
Yes. We are becoming more aware that development is not just about numbers and targets. There are people behind every service point that is built. When we see people in remote areas finally being able to access the internet, children can access information to learn, health workers can communicate faster, or government offices can provide better services, we see the true meaning of connectivity development. That is what makes me feel that this work must be escorted to the end.
If you can summarize, what is your message about the development of Indonesian connectivity?
"In my opinion, connectivity must be seen as part of efforts to provide more equal opportunities for the community. Do not let geographical location determine whether someone can get access to good information, education, health, or public services.
Therefore, infrastructure development must always go hand in hand with strong governance, good supervision, and most importantly, ensuring that the benefits are truly felt by the community. In the end, we are not just building a network. We are paving the way so that people everywhere can have the same opportunity to develop.
There was a time when Virgie Baker was used to chasing the news, moving from one location to another, meeting many people, and finding answers directly from the field. For about 25 years as a journalist, the world became part of his daily life. However, when he later transformed into a Supervisory Board, he had to enter a completely different space.
"The discussion is very difficult. It's very technical," recalled Virgie when describing his initial impression as a Supervisory Board.
He is not ashamed to admit that he was surprised. In the meeting room, various technical terms and abbreviations come and go. For people who are involved in the world of technology every day, these terms may sound familiar. However, for Virgie, everything takes time to understand.
Instead of feeling intimidated, he chose to ask.
Every time he finds an abbreviation he doesn't understand, he immediately asks for an explanation. After the first meeting, he even asked the internal team to provide a kind of short course on basic things related to his work. "One day I learned it, I just understood. Oh, it turns out it's not as complicated as I imagined," he said.
According to him, the biggest challenge at first was not the technology itself, but the technical language used to explain it. Once the terms were understood, the work became much easier.
He was also helped by experts and internal teams who provided basic knowledge support. From there, Virgie began to find ways to combine his past experience as a journalist with his new role as a supervisor.
And it turns out, the two are not too different.
The world of journalism taught him one important thing: don't just believe what's written on paper. Therefore, when carrying out his duties as a Supervisory Board, Virgie Baker feels more comfortable when he goes directly to the field. "Because I used to be a journalist, I definitely go directly to the field more," he said.
In the field, he again did what has been his habit for decades: looking for information, listening to the community, seeing problems up close, as well as receiving criticism and input.
For him, the experience was actually fun.
The journalistic spirit that has been formed for years has not disappeared. Only the place and responsibility have changed.
His first assignment even took him to Kupang Regency, East Nusa Tenggara. From the city center, the journey still has to continue for about three hours to a more remote area. Such a journey made him see Indonesia from a different angle.
During 25 years as a journalist, Virgie has become accustomed to traveling to various regions. Therefore, he can feel the changes that occur from time to time. Cities that used to feel deserted are now growing more crowded. Infrastructure is developing. Public access is also becoming more open. "The changes are now almost the same in the regions," he said.
However, the experience of going to remote areas also made him understand that development cannot only be seen from the city center. There are people who live far from the center of government, far from access to services, and need the presence of the state in a tangible form.
That's where the role of supervision, according to Virgie, gets its meaning.
"Not just looking at reports, but ensuring that what is built is really felt by the community.
In the midst of his busy schedule, there is one role that he never left: being a mother. High mobility is actually not new for Virgie Baker's family. During his time as a journalist, his children were used to seeing their mother go on duty.
Even when the children were small, Virgie still tried to carry out her responsibilities as a mother. He still remembers how he brought equipment to express and store breast milk when he had to travel. "I remember then I took the breast milk backpack everywhere," he recalled.
Busy work does not make him want to eliminate the role. He still tries to carry out his responsibilities as a mother, including breastfeeding until his children are two years old. Now, when his role changes to the Supervisory Board, the principle is still the same.
According to Virgie, no matter how busy a mother is, her duties to the family should not be missed. "The important thing is that these tasks are not skipped," he said.
He is grateful to have a husband and children who provide support. His children are also used to being independent when their mother has to be out of town. When Virgie is at home, they can enjoy togetherness. However, when work takes him away, the children understand and are able to carry out their own activities.
Still, there is a simple happiness that is always awaited.
When Virgie can go home early and pick up the children from school activities, for example, their faces will light up. For Virgie, simple moments like that are actually an important part of life balance.
Every Sunday, after worship, Virgie Baker tries to find time to get together. In the midst of work demands, she believes that the quality of family time is not always determined by how long it takes. The important thing is to be present when the opportunity is there.

title: World Bank: Poor Internet, Idle Spectrum, and Infrastructure Disconnected - Kompas.id
snippet: World Bank: Poor Internet, Idle Spectrum, and Infrastructure Disconnected Kompas.id
article_text:
With internet penetration only at 72.8 percent and low network quality, Indonesia faces a digital paradox.
16 Des 2025 16:54 WIB · English
Share
Copy Link
By Caecilia Mediana
JAKARTA, KOMPAS — Digitalization has become one of the keys to accelerating national economic growth. However, in reality, Indonesia is facing fundamental issues: the quality of the internet is among the worst in the region, strategic frequency spectrum is underutilized, and digital infrastructure has not been managed as a national asset.
This is one of the strategic issues highlighted in the World Bank's latest report, "Indonesia Economic Prospects: A Digital Foundation for Growth," released in Jakarta on Tuesday (December 16, 2025).
Jonathan Marskell, the World Bank's Senior Digital Specialist for Indonesia and Timor Leste, told Kompas in Jakarta that digitalization could be a key factor in accelerating the national economy. However, Indonesia's digital infrastructure development still has work to do.
As many as 72.8 percent of the Indonesian population has accessed the internet. The remaining 27.2 percent have not yet gained access. For those who are already connected to the internet, the majority still face low quality and speed.
Indonesia's internet speed is the lowest among upper-middle-income countries. Among ASEAN countries, Indonesia ranks third or fourth from the bottom.
From the perspective of mobile telecommunications services, the main issue lies in the limited amount of frequency spectrum owned by operators. This problem also causes mobile telecommunications operators in Indonesia to transition fully to 5G at a slow pace.
Indonesia allocates the least spectrum for mobile internet among G-20 countries and ranks fourth lowest among Asia-Pacific nations. Meanwhile, the government possesses strategic spectrum bands that have not been optimally utilized and could be auctioned off soon to encourage improvements in internet speed and network investment.
"There are two frequency spectrums that should be auctioned off soon, namely 700 megahertz (MHz) and 2.6 gigahertz (GHz). However, for some reason, the auction for 700 MHz has been delayed for three years. Meanwhile, the 2.6 GHz frequency spectrum, which was recently acquired by the government on January 1, 2025, is still 'idle' or has not yet been auctioned," he said.
The government possesses strategic spectrum bands that have not been optimally utilized and can be auctioned off soon to encourage the enhancement of internet speed and network investment.
Another important frequency spectrum is 3.5 GHz. Currently, a portion is allocated for the use of satellite automated teller machines (ATMs). The World Bank observes that in urban areas, ATM machines should be able to utilize internet network infrastructure access outside of satellite connections.
Thus, the Government of Indonesia should be able to allocate part of the bandwidth of the 3.5 GHz frequency spectrum for the deployment of 5G in urban areas. For the remaining portion, the government can allocate it for ATMs in rural areas.
Still related to the frequency spectrum for mobile telecommunications services, the World Bank also observes that Indonesia imposes relatively high usage fees. The frequency spectrum costs in Indonesia account for 11.4 percent of revenue. This is higher compared to Thailand at only 9 percent, Malaysia at 3.6 percent, and the Philippines at 1.9 percent.
Regarding internet access generated by fixed broadband networks, the World Bank states that 39 million homes, or nearly half of all households, are within reach of a fixed broadband network. However, only 17.4 million are connected to the network.
In fact, almost all households have access to electricity. This condition indicates that the challenge does not lie in the availability of infrastructure, but in affordability.
"The fixed broadband internet service market is dominated by one major player. Network development through infrastructure sharing schemes is still limited. Fiber-optic networks have not yet reached many villages, as our data shows that only 50 percent of villages have fiber-optic connections. As a result, internet quality and affordability remain low," said Jonathan.
The Indonesian government has actually developed the Palapa Ring backbone telecommunications infrastructure for the western, central, and eastern packages. The project was carried out under the Government and Business Entity Cooperation (KPBU) scheme.
However, according to a World Bank study, the three Palapa Ring projects are not interconnected, nor are they connected to other backbone networks owned by the private sector. Furthermore, the wholesale rental price of the Palapa Ring project is excessively high.
As a result, the utilization rate of Palapa Ring is not optimal. This situation, according to Jonathan, is one of the main reasons why the cost of internet access in Papua remains high.
Referring to the same report, the World Bank assesses that the government has not optimally utilized the public-private partnership satellite project named Satria-1. With a total capacity of 150 Gbps, Satria-1 was initially aimed at connecting 150,000 public service points in underserved and unserved areas across Indonesia.
After the launch, the target locations were reduced to 50,000 points and then to 37,000 points. The installation has been progressing well in accordance with this adjusted scope, with 27,805 locations connected by mid-2025.
However, about three-fifths of the locations activated with Satria-1 are in Sumatra, Java, and Sulawesi. These are areas where terrestrial fiber optic deployment and fixed wireless access are feasible and more optimal.
"Meanwhile, less than 12 percent of the area covered by Satria-1 is located in Papua and Maluku. In this region, the population is sparse and the challenging terrain makes satellites the most effective solution for telecommunications access," he stated.
The launch of the low-orbit satellite owned by billionaire Elon Musk in 2024, namely Starlink, according to the World Bank, has a positive impact on the Indonesian internet market. Demand is increasing rapidly.
This is not only happening in rural areas with limited networks but also in large cities that have experienced overcapacity. Although the rates are relatively high, the strong interest indicates a significant demand for faster and more reliable internet.
The World Bank report also mentions data centers. The World Bank states that the capacity of data centers in Indonesia is the third largest in Southeast Asia, after Malaysia and Singapore. However, Indonesia's competitiveness is lagging behind because neighboring countries are moving more aggressively.
In Indonesia, data center investment is hindered by several issues. First, the licensing process is complicated and can take one to two years. Second, there is regulatory uncertainty regarding data—particularly concerning personal data protection and cross-border data flows. Third, there are limitations in supporting infrastructure such as electricity.
As a result, many global investors choose to build data centers in Malaysia or Thailand, even though the largest market is actually in Indonesia.
"Furthermore, the landing of international submarine telecommunications cables tends to be concentrated in Jakarta. This has the potential to diminish investment attractiveness. The government is advised to open access to submarine cables to other economic centers in Indonesia," said Jonathan.
Based on these various tasks, the World Bank recommends several things to the Indonesian government. From a mobile telecommunications perspective, the government could not only reduce spectrum costs and lost revenue, but also combine operator performance obligations and infrastructure coverage. The government should also encourage active and passive sharing of fixed broadband infrastructure.
The World Bank also recommended that the government review the Palapa Ring project, including rental rates and fiberization. Regarding low-orbit telecommunications satellites, the World Bank believes they are best suited to serve rural and maritime areas. Meanwhile, geostationary satellites remain crucial for backhaul, broadcasting, and public facility connectivity in remote areas.
The President Director and CEO of Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison, Vikram Sinha, while attending the launch of the World Bank report, argued that the Indonesian government must view digital infrastructure as a strategic national infrastructure. Thus, the government will always prioritize the cost and speed of development time.
"Please, the government needs to act more quickly. In terms of frequency spectrum, for example, the government has promised to auction 3.5 GHz. However, in the roadmap, it is scheduled for auction in 2028, which will not assist mobile telecommunications operators," he said.
Vikram emphasized that without support from digital infrastructure, efforts to achieve the goal of 8 percent economic growth will not be optimal. Improvements and equitable distribution of digital infrastructure require numerous partnership schemes between the government and business entities.
At the same opportunity, the Director General of Digital Ecosystem at the Ministry of Communication and Digital (Kemenkomdigi), Edwin Hidayat Abdullah, stated that Indonesia contributes approximately 40 percent of the digital economy in Asia, yet its potential has not been optimally harnessed. The government proposed a 6C framework as a strategy to strengthen the digital ecosystem.
The strategy in question includes connectivity, cloud computing, and cybersecurity as the foundation of digital infrastructure. There's also capital, namely layered funding for research, startups, and MSMEs. Next comes capability and the supply chain for digital talent development.
Commerce, which uses data as an asset for economic development. Compliance, which creates adaptive regulations that support innovation. Catalyst, which means the government plays a role in creating markets and demand for innovation.
"To accelerate an inclusive innovation ecosystem, we are launching the Garuda Spark Innovation Hub initiative, which integrates research, industry, talent, and funding on a national scale while being locally adaptive," said Edwin.
